topic_text: The value of goods and services produced in the UK.
text:
UK real gross domestic product (GDP) is estimated to have increased by 0.4% in Quarter 2 (Apr to Jun) 2026, following growth of 0.6% in Quarter 1 (Jan to Mar) 2026.

In output terms, growth in the latest quarter was caused by a 0.5% increase in the services sector and an increase of 0.3% in the construction sector.

Real GDP per head is estimated to have increased by 0.4% in Quarter 2 2026, and is up 1.0% compared with the same quarter a year ago.

topic_text: How much the production and services industries contribute to economic output.
text:
Production output was estimated to have decreased (down 0.5%) during the three months to July 2026, compared with the three months to April 2026; this is the first fall in the three-month-on-three-month series since November 2025 (down 0.5%).

Of the four main sectors in the three months to July 2026, negative contributions came from "water supply and sewerage" (down 4.0%), "electricity and gas" (down 1.5%) and "mining and quarrying" (down 2.6%); this was partially offset by a rise from "manufacturing" (up 0.5%).

Monthly production output was estimated to have increased by 0.2% in July 2026; this follows decreases in June 2026 (down 0.2%) and May 2026 (down 0.7%).

There were increases in monthly production in July 2026 for "manufacturing" (up 0.9%) and "water supply and sewerage" (up 2.0%); these were partially offset by decreases in "mining and quarrying" (down 4.4%) and "electricity and gas" (down 1.5%).

Services output for the three months to July 2026 was estimated to have increased by 0.6%, compared with the three months to April 2026.

In the three months to July 2026, 11 of the 14 sectors saw a rise, with the main positive contributing sectors being “professional, scientific and technical activities” (up by 2.1%), followed by “information and communication” (up by 2.5%).

Monthly services output was estimated to have increased by 0.4% in July 2026; this follows increases in June 2026 (up by 0.4%) and May 2026 (up by 0.1%).

There were monthly increases in 8 of the 14 sectors in July 2026, with the largest positive contributions on the month coming from "administrative and support service activities" (up by 3.7%) and "information and communication" (up by 2.4%); this was largely because of the continuation of strong growth from "computer programming, consultancy and related activities" (up by 3.5%).

topic_text: Measures of demand in the economy for output that is produced.
text:
The quantity of goods bought (volume) in retail sales is estimated to have risen by 0.9% in the three months to August 2026 compared with the three months to May 2026. Non-store retailers’ sales volumes rose following a particularly strong June period, while food stores did well across the latest three months.

Retail sales volumes are estimated to have risen by 0.5% in August 2026. This follows a fall of 0.5% in July 2026 (unrevised from our previous bulletin), and a rise of 0.6% in June 2026 (revised down from a 0.7% rise in our previous bulletin). Non-store retailers partially recovered from falls in July 2026, with lower sales volumes in July attributed to promotions occurring earlier in June 2026. Department stores also picked up in August following stock availability issues in July.

UK business investment increased by 0.9% in Quarter 1 (Jan to Mar) 2026, revised up from a 0.7% increase in the provisional estimate.

The largest contributors to the increase in business investment was transport, with a smaller contribution from other buildings and structures.

UK business investment is 1.3% below the level seen in the same quarter a year ago.

UK business investment has increased by 4.3% annually for 2025.

UK whole economy investment (technically known as gross fixed capital formation (GFCF)), which includes business and public sector investment, increased by 0.4% in Quarter 1 2026; this was revised up from a 0.6% decrease in the provisional estimate.

UK GFCF is 1.6% above the level seen in the same quarter a year ago.

topic_text: Changes in prices of goods and services bought by consumers, as well as those bought and sold by producers in the UK.
text:
The Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs (CPIH) 12-month inflation rate was 3.3% in August 2026, up from 3.1% in July 2026.

Consumer price inflation can be influenced by the strength of domestic supply and demand, and changes in the UK prices of imports. The inflation rate also depends on price levels in the preceding year.

Changes in the output Producer Price Index inflation rate can be influenced by changes in labour and energy costs.

Producer output (factory gate) prices rose by 3.7% in the year to August 2026, up from a revised rise of 3.3% in the year to July.

Producer input prices rose by 6.1% in the year to August 2026, up from a revised rise of 5.8% in the year to July.

Input prices are influenced by raw material prices and exchange rate movements so are more changeable over time than output prices.

topic_text: UK exports and imports of goods and services and measures of foreign direct investment.
text:
The value of goods imports rose by £1.3 billion (2.4%) in July 2026, with a rise in imports from non-EU countries partially offset by a fall in imports from the EU.

The value of goods exports rose by £0.9 billion (2.8%) in July 2026, with increases in exports to both EU and non-EU countries.

The total goods and services trade deficit narrowed by £1.1 billion to £9.0 billion in the three months to July 2026, compared with the three months to April 2026.

The trade in goods deficit narrowed by £0.4 billion to £61.6 billion in the three months to July 2026, while the trade in services surplus is estimated to have widened by £0.7 billion to £52.6 billion.

measure: FDI - liabilities (overseas investment into the UK)
text: UK direct investment liabilities were £2,223.7 billion in January to March 2026, down from £2,255.3 billion in the previous quarter. FDI liabilities have been following a broadly downward trend in the last two years.

UK direct investment assets were £2,120.2 billion in January to March 2026, down from £2,137.1 billion in the previous quarter. The value of FDI assets has been following a broadly downward trend since early 2023.
